text:
On Wednesday afternoon, Hassan was in the office kitchen when a coworker burned her hand on the kettle. Hassan grabbed his phone. "Hey assistant, how long should I run cold water on a burn?" he asked. The assistant said to hold the burn under cool running water for at least ten minutes, and not to use ice. Hassan helped her to the sink.
Then he said, "Read me the steps for a small burn." The assistant read them slowly: cool the burn, cover it with a clean, loose bandage, and do not pop any blisters. The first aid box on the wall was almost empty, so Hassan said, "Put bandages on my shopping list." The assistant put them on the list.
After a while his coworker felt well again. Hassan remembered that the company had spent two thousand dollars on safety training last year, but the box still needed a refill. He asked the assistant to remind him on Friday to buy more supplies.

Person: Can you tell me when the water bill is due and remind me two days before?
Assistant: Sure. Which water company is it with?
Person: The city one. I forget the brand of the meter, but the bill comes from the city.
Assistant: Got it. The city water bill is due on the twentieth. I will remind you on the eighteenth.
Person: Great. Can you also pay my rent from my savings?
Assistant: I am sorry, I can't make payments. I can point you to the rent due date and remind you to pay it yourself.
Person: Okay, please remind me. I want a quiet evening without worrying.
Assistant: Done. I will remind you on the first at six in the evening.

Tariq was peeling oranges for the kids when the kitchen got too loud. The twins were shouting about a cartoon, and the baby was crying. He had no free hand, so he spoke to the speaker on the shelf. "Play something calm, and turn it down a bit," he said.
The speaker started a soft piano playlist and lowered the volume. Tariq smiled. "Skip this one, it sounds sad," he added a minute later, and the speaker jumped to the next song.
The kids slowed down and listened. After a stretch of quiet, the oldest girl asked for something with drums. "Play a dozen songs with drums," Tariq said. The speaker made a short playlist of twelve songs and began the first one. Tariq finished the oranges and put them on the table, and the whole family ate in a good mood.

A contact is a small card in your phone with a name, a number, and sometimes an address or a birthday. It helps you call or write to people without remembering every number. Often you need to change a card. A friend moves, so you say, "Update Lena's address." A sister gets a new phone, so you say, "Change Dad's number to this one." If a strange number calls and you want to keep it, you say, "Save this number as the plumber." Some people keep numbers on paper inside a backpack, but a saved contact is easier to find. You can also say, "Delete the old number for Sam" or "Fix the spelling of Maria's name." With a saved card, nobody has to cry over a lost number.

People want to change how many servings a recipe makes, even on a busy night when the scale's charger is dead.
Halve it
Make this for two
Can you trim this recipe in half?
I only need six portions, not twelve
Double everything, we have guests
How much flour do I need for three people instead of eight?
Turn the pancake recipe into one for four servings
Could you please scale the soup recipe up to ten servings for me, because my cousins are coming over?

Rizal sat on the porch with a cup of tea and a calendar full of circles. He was a retired teacher, and he liked to count things. "Assistant, how many days until my granddaughter's birthday on the fourth of July?" he asked.
The assistant counted and said there were thirty-one days left. Rizal nodded. "And how old will she be?" The assistant said she would turn nine.
He felt a free afternoon stretching out in front of him, so he asked one more thing. "Tell me how many days are in the school holiday, from June first to August twelfth." The assistant did the sums and answered with seventy-three days.
Rizal wrote the number on the back of a jar label and stuck it to the fridge. Then he put the dishes in the sink to wash, humming, and went to look for a gift.

Kasia was making dinner for forty guests at the restaurant, and the butter had not come. She stirred the pot and looked at the clock. "I'm running out of butter, and nothing has arrived yet," she said to her phone.
The assistant understood that she wanted to know about her order. It opened her last order and said the box of butter was still on the truck, with six stops to go. A little meter on the screen showed the delivery was about half done.
Kasia felt sad for a moment. "Can you tell the driver to hurry?" she asked. The assistant said it could not do that, but it could send her a message the moment the truck was close. Kasia agreed. She used the last bit of butter on the first pan and waited, and twenty minutes later her phone buzzed that the truck was outside.

name: tune_drink
does: Makes a drink stronger, weaker, sweeter or less sweet, and starts the machine to run a fresh cup after a short nap in the morning.
inputs: which drink it is, and whether to make it stronger, weaker, sweeter or less sweet
people say:
- Make my coffee stronger
- Less sugar in my tea, please
- This smoothie is too sweet
- I barely slept, I need something with more kick
- Can you make it a bit milder?
- Same as yesterday, but sweeter

Giulia sat on her bed with her phone, looking at a pair of pants in an online shop from London. The price said fifty pounds. She texted the assistant. "how much is 50 pounds in euros? i don't want a long answer, just the number"
The assistant answered with one short line: about fifty-eight euros. Giulia frowned. "is there a nearby shop that sells the same pants? not online, i don't want to wait for shipping"
The assistant looked and found a store ten minutes away by bus. It showed the opening hours and said it closed at eight. Giulia sat up. "ok save that store to my places and remind me to go tomorrow after school," she wrote. The assistant saved the store and set the reminder for four o'clock the next day. Giulia put the phone down, happy that she did not have to pay for shipping.

A parent wants screens to end at a set time, so the kids can go outside or sit by the fireplace while dinner gets a stir.
Turn off the tablets at five
Screen time is over before lunch on Sunday
Stop the TV for the kids at half past six tonight
Can you shut down the game console after supper on Friday?
Lock the kids' tablets until tomorrow morning
I want the screens off by the time the soup is ready on Saturday
Please switch off the children's devices at seven every school night so they have time to play and get ready for bed
Tell the kids it's time to stop, and cut the wifi in their rooms before lunch on Sunday

Ananya, a retired teacher, sat at the kitchen table with her square tin of tea leaves. She had won a small prize at the village fair for her ginger tea, and she wanted to make it again. She typed quickly on her tablet: "make my tea strnger and save it as my usual"
The assistant understood her typing. It told her it had made the next cup stronger by a little, then saved the new setting under the name "my usual." Ananya smiled and pressed the button on the kettle.
"Can you also make it less sweet next time?" she asked out loud. The assistant said it would lower the sugar by one spoon from now on. When the tea was ready, it was just right, and Ananya poured it into her best cup and sat by the window to enjoy it.

name: park_time_left
does: Tells you how many minutes are left on your parking and how many dollars it costs to extend it, so a strange street never leads to a ticket.
inputs: the car plate or spot number, and the street or lot name
people say:
- How long do I have left?
- Am I about to get a ticket?
- Keep my parking going for another hour
- I don't want to cry over a fine, check my time
- What do I owe for this spot?
- Tell me when it's about to run out

Marlene sat down with her breakfast and a mug of tea. She was not good with technology, and the little smart speaker on the table still confused her. But she wanted to hear her book. In a gentle voice she said, "Read book."
The speaker answered, "Do you want to continue your audiobook, The Garden Letters?" Marlene said yes. The speaker found the place where she stopped the night before and started playing from chapter six.
A few minutes later the narrator spoke too fast. "Slower," said Marlene. The speaker lowered the speed a little. When the doorbell rang, she said, "Pause." The speaker stopped at once. After she talked with the neighbor, she said, "Come back," and the story went on from the same sentence. Marlene was pleased, and she finished her toast while the story continued.

Giulia worked as a cook in a small cafe, and her days were long. On Sunday she remembered that her sister's birthday was in November, and she felt a push of worry. She did not want to forget again.
"Remind me to buy a present for my sister next Tuesday at noon," she said to her phone. The assistant set the reminder and said it would remind her at twelve o'clock.
"Also, what could I get her? She likes plants and tea," Giulia asked. The assistant listed a few ideas: a small herb pot, a box of mint tea, or a pretty cup. Giulia liked the pot and the tea together.
"Put those two on my list," she said. The assistant did. Giulia felt happy and went back to chopping onions, sure that this year the gift would come on time.

Person: put on the cookin show
Assistant: Sure. Which channel is it on?
Person: i dont remember. its the one with the lady who makes cream cakes
Assistant: I can scan the guide for cooking shows. I found one called Sweet Hands on channel twelve. Is that the one?
Person: yes thats it. and turn on the subtitels
Assistant: Done. The subtitles are on. Do you want me to record the next episode too?
Person: yes please. last time i missed it and the cake was stale by the time i saw the recipe
Assistant: I will record it every Thursday at seven.

A work meeting is a time when people join one call to talk, share their screens, and follow an agenda. The agenda is a short list of what will be discussed, and it keeps things from running long. People often ask to change a meeting. If a morning meeting is too early, someone says, "Move it to ten." If a colleague is late, they say, "Push it back by fifteen minutes." If you need to rush to join, you can say, "Join my next call." During the call, people say, "Share my screen" or "Mute me." A false start can happen when the link is wrong, so people also ask, "Send me the right link again."

Darius stood outside the clinic with his keys in his hand and a sour feeling in his stomach. He was late for the dentist and had parked in a hurry. He had only ten minutes left on his ticket, and he had just eaten a boiled egg that tasted bad.
"I only have ten minutes on my parking, and my appointment is an hour long," he told his phone.
The assistant understood that he needed more time. It opened the parking app, found his spot on Elm Street, and asked, "Do you want to extend it by one hour?" Darius said yes. The assistant paid for the extra time and showed the new end time on the screen. Then it set a reminder ten minutes before the end. Darius could point his thoughts at his teeth and nothing else.

In a cold town, people who prefer a warm house, and wear a sour face on frosty mornings, ask for the heating to go up.
Warmer, please
Set it to seventy
It's freezing in here
Turn the thermostat up a little
Make the living room warmer before I wake up
Can you get the house to seventy-two by six this evening?
The bedroom is cold, can you heat it for half an hour?
I would really like the radiators on in the morning, because the baby gets cold easily

Person: wen is the next bus to the plant market
Assistant: I can look that up. Which bus stop are you at?
Person: the one by the church on Mill Road
Assistant: The next bus from Mill Road is number fourteen, in six minutes. It stops at the plant market.
Person: ok. can you forward that to my daughter?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't send messages to other people. I can show you the time on your screen.
Person: fine. i just need to stay calm and not run. my dryer is still on at home
Assistant: I can turn the dryer off if it is a smart one. Is it connected to the app?
Person: yes it is
Assistant: Done. The dryer is off.

Adam did not like gadgets, but his daughter had set up a speaker in the living room and told him to try it. He stood on the lovely wool rug in his socks and spoke loudly. "Start my morning workout and keep time for me."
The speaker said, "Starting a ten minute workout. Ready?" Adam said yes. It counted twenty squats and then ten push-ups, and Adam huffed. In the middle he got tired. "Slow down and give me a rest," he said. The speaker gave him thirty seconds to breathe.
At the end, Adam asked how many days of rest he should take before the next workout. The speaker said one day was a good idea. It also asked if it should keep a record of the workout. "Yes, please," said Adam. Down by the river, his daughter later saw his smile on a photo.

Anh was in the garden planting beans when a sharp pain shot through her tooth. She felt it every time she bit down. She wiped her hands on her apron and took out her phone.
"Book dentist," she said.
The assistant asked, "Which dentist? Do you want Dr. Park, whom you saw last year?" Anh nodded. "Yes, Dr. Park. Soonest," she said.
The assistant looked at the calendar and found a free spot on Thursday at ten. It was at the clinic on the west side of town. "Shall I book that?" it asked. Anh said, "Yes." The assistant booked it and put a note in her calendar. Then it asked if she wanted a reminder the night before. Anh said yes, and went back to her beans, feeling better already.

Zeynep sat at her desk and heard a sound from her phone. A stranger had tried to connect to her bluetooth speaker again. She worried about her privacy. It was a bad habit of the neighbor's laptop, but she did not want anyone to see her photos.
"Block every new device that tries to connect to my phone," she told the assistant. The assistant turned on a setting so that only the devices she had approved could connect. It showed her three old devices on the list and asked which ones to remove.
"Remove the two I don't use," said Zeynep. The assistant removed them. Then she asked it to lock her phone with a longer passcode, double the length of the old one. The assistant guided her through the new passcode, and Zeynep felt safer.

People want a measurement changed into other units, such as the weight of a damp towel or the distance to a village.
how many ounzes in a pound
km to miles
remind me how many cups are in a quart
whats 30 celsius in fahrenheit
how long is a mile in meters
convert 5 feet to centimeters
tell me how heavy two kilos are in pounds
Could you please tell me how many liters are in a gallon, because I am following a recipe from abroad?

Tala woke up to a loud noise outside her window. She rubbed her eyes and heard a truck on the highway nearby. She was waiting for a package, and today was supposed to be the day. She still lay in bed with the blanket up to her chin.
"I think the truck is outside, but I don't hear anyone at the door," she said to her phone.
The assistant guessed that she wanted to know about the delivery. It checked her order and said the package was out for delivery, due between nine and noon. It was now the middle of the morning. The driver had tried to shout up to her flat, the note said, but nobody had answered.
Tala jumped up. "Ask them to come back," she said. The assistant sent a message asking the driver to try again, and Tala hurried to the door in her socks.

name: lawn_status
does: Tells you if the robot mower is outside cutting the grass, and can send it home when you hear a horn or rain starts.
inputs: which mower, and whether you want to know its status or send it back
people say:
- Is the mower still cutting?
- Send the robot home, it's about to rain
- Did the lawn get mowed today?
- I hear the mower beeping, what's wrong?
- Stop cutting the grass, we have guests
- Where is the mower right now?

Rosa came home after a long night shift at the hospital. Her eyes were heavy, but she remembered the electricity bill. She stood in the hallway, holding her mop, and talked to her phone.
"Remind me to pay the electric bill every Monday at nine until I tell you to stop," she said.
The assistant said, "Every Monday at nine, starting this Monday. Is that right?" Rosa said yes. Then she frowned. "I think there's an old reminder about the water bill that I don't need now. Delete it." The assistant found it and deleted it.
"Do you want to see your bills with special due dates this month?" it asked. Rosa nodded. The assistant read out two bills: the electric bill, due on the fifteenth, and the phone bill, due on the twenty-second. Rosa thanked it, put away the mop, and finally went to bed.

A grocery list is a short list of things you need to buy. It saves you from forgetting milk or eggs and from buying too much. People keep it in a phone, on the fridge, or in a notebook. When you run out of something, you say, "Put eggs on the list." When you buy it, you say, "Take eggs off." If the list gets mixed up, you can say, "Restart the list" and start fresh. At the least, a good list says what you need and how much. Before the weekend people also ask, "What is in the fridge?" or "What do we need for dinner?" On a trip to the sea, they say, "Make a list for a picnic."

People want to compare their electricity bills from this month and last month, and see why one cheese-shop-sized bill went up in the south apartment.
Compare my bills
How does this month's bill look next to last month's?
Was the electric bill higher in January?
Show me this bill and last year's bill side by side
Did the water bill go up since spring?
Why is my power bill so much bigger now?
Could you please compare the last three electricity bills for me? I think the price went up and I want to ask the company about it.
I would be grateful if you could line up this year's heating bills with last year's, since I'm trying to decide whether to move to a smaller place.

Person: Can you start the mower?
Assistant: Sure. Which mower do you mean, the front lawn or the back lawn?
Person: The back one. My mom wants it done before dinner.
Assistant: Okay. How short should I cut the grass?
Person: A bit shorter than last time. Maybe half an inch less.
Assistant: Got it. I will cut it half an inch shorter. Starting now.
Person: Can you also scroll through the weather and tell me if it will rain tonight?
Assistant: I can check. It says no rain tonight, but more clouds in the morning.
Person: Thanks. Can you water the roses too?
Assistant: I am sorry, I can't water plants by hand. I can turn on the sprinklers for ten minutes if you like.

Baking turns flour, water, yeast and sugar into bread, cakes and cookies. Each recipe has a time for the dough to rest and rise, and a time for the oven. People often change the plan. If a cake looks too brown, they say, "Dim the oven" or "Lower the heat to a hundred and fifty." If the dough is slow, they ask, "Add ten more minutes to the timer." Many bakers buy flour from a local mill and mix it in a blender or with their hands. When the cookies are ready, they say, "Stop the timer," or "How long until the bread is done?" The words are simple, but they help the oven and the baker work together.

A phone is a small computer that you carry. It has a battery, a bright screen and room for photos and apps. People change a few settings every day. If the screen hurts their eyes, they say, "Make the screen dimmer." If they are in a meeting, they say, "Turn on do not disturb." When the phone is almost full, they ask, "How much storage is left?" and "Delete my old photos." If a guest wants to use the wifi, they say, "Show me the wifi password." People also ask the phone to search for things, like "Search for a pizza place nearby." When the battery is low, they say, "Turn on battery saver," so an old phone can last all day.

Roya was not good with technology, but she knew she needed a new password. Her grandson had told her that a good password was long and not easy to guess. She sat in her blue armchair and looked at the tablet.
"Excuse me, assistant, would you please help me change my email password? A man phoned me from the mall yesterday and asked many questions, and now I'm worried," she said politely.
The assistant said it was glad to help. It asked her to name a new password that she would remember, and it explained that she should not use a birthday. Roya chose a line from her favorite song. The assistant checked that it was strong enough and saved it in the password list. It also told her never to give the password to anyone on the phone. Roya felt much better.

An emergency is when something goes wrong fast, like smoke in the kitchen, a power cut, or water on the floor. Homes have a few simple helpers. A smoke alarm makes a loud sound when it senses smoke. A flashlight helps in a power cut. Many families keep a plain list of numbers on the fridge. People can also ask a phone for help. They say, "Call for help," "Call my mother," or "Where is the nearest hospital?" After a flood, they might say, "Turn off the water." It is good to practice before a real emergency. A bucket of water might weigh many pounds, and a gallon of water weighs about eight, so people should move slowly and ask for help.

Francesca, a grandmother, took her pills every morning, but lately she forgot the second one in the evening. Her granddaughter had put a smart display on the kitchen counter, and Francesca decided to try it.
"Remind me to take my blue pill every evening at eight," she said.
The display answered, "I will remind you every evening at eight. Do you want the reminder to be louder than your alarm?" Francesca said, "A little louder, yes." The display made the sound a bit louder.
Then she remembered her car. "Also remind me weekly to check the tire air. And if I say later, wait half an hour," she said. The display agreed. It would remind her every Saturday morning about the tire. Francesca felt proud. Now she did not have to lower her head in shame at the doctor's when she forgot.

Person: It is so cold in this post office, I can hardly think.
Assistant: I'm sorry to hear that. I can't control the heat in the post office, but I can find a warmer place nearby. Do you want that?
Person: No, I need to stay. I have to send a box. How do I know the cost?
Assistant: I can look up the price. How much does the box weigh?
Person: I don't know. Everyone at home says it is heavy. Maybe I should subtract the weight of the box from the total?
Assistant: I can subtract it if you tell me both numbers. What does the scale say?
Person: Four pounds total, and the box is one pound.
Assistant: Then the things inside weigh three pounds. Shipping will be about eight dollars. I hope that makes you happy.

People want to know the next step of a baking recipe, when the dough is quiet and resting, and they need to pull the tray out at the right time.
What's next?
Next step
Tell me the next step
What do I do now with the dough?
I'm done kneading, now what?
Is the dough ready for the oven?
When should I pull the cookies out, and what do I do after that?
Could you please read me the next step of the bread recipe? My hands are covered in flour.

name: cool_room
does: Closes the blinds and starts the fan or air conditioner in one room when a sudden heat wave makes it too warm, and can send you a document with the room's temperatures.
inputs: which room, and how cool you want it
people say:
- It's boiling in the bedroom
- Cool down the living room to seventy
- The sun is heating up the kitchen
- Can you make the office cooler before I get there?
- Turn on the fan upstairs
- Shut the blinds and cool the baby's room

Rizal woke up late, with his hair in all directions and his mouth dry. The fan above the bed was still turning. He remembered, with a jolt, that his car was parked on a street with a two hour limit, and it had been three. He took the phone from the table, and he did not want to wash his face yet.
"Excuse me, assistant, could you please tell me how much time I have left on my parking? I fell asleep and I'm afraid I got a ticket. I need to know the true situation before I go outside," he said.
The assistant checked and said the parking had run out forty minutes ago, but no ticket had been marked yet. It offered to pay for another hour. Rizal said yes, thanked it, and ran out to move his car.

A to-do list is a list of tasks you want to finish. It helps you remember them and see what is left. Some people keep it on paper, and others in a phone. Each task can have a priority, which means how important it is. A healthy habit is to check things off when they are done. People often change their lists with short words. They say, "Put call the dentist on my list," "Move laundry to tomorrow," or "Mark the report as done." At the end of the week, someone might say, "Empty the list" to remove old tasks. They might also ask, "What is on my list today?" or "What is the most important thing?" Even a microwave reminder, like heating lunch, can go on the list.

Person: Take a picture of the cake and send it to my sister.
Assistant: Sure. Which sister, Anna or Rosa?
Person: Anna. And please make the ugly corner of the cake look better, because I wonder if she'll laugh.
Assistant: I can take the photo and send it to Anna, but I can't fix the cake in the picture. Do you want me to crop the corner out?
Person: Yes, crop it, and put the picture in the album called Birthday.
Assistant: Done. The photo is cropped and sent to Anna, and it is in the Birthday album.
Person: Great. There's some corn on the table too, can you zoom in?
Assistant: I'm sorry, the picture is already taken. I can take a new one if you like.

name: swap_meetings
does: Swaps the times of two events in your calendar, and it can be automatic if you want it to keep the free time for lunch with lettuce and sandwiches.
inputs: the two events, and the new times, or just the days to swap
people say:
- Put my dentist visit where the haircut is
- Switch Monday's call with Tuesday's
- Can you flip my lunch and my meeting?
- I need the afternoon free, move that to tomorrow
- Trade places for the yoga class and the school pickup

name: fan_restart
does: Restarts a fan or cooling unit that has stopped, so the room goes back to a perfect temperature and the song of the fan returns.
inputs: which fan or cooler, and how long to run it
people say:
- The fan stopped working
- It's hot again, the air conditioner is off
- Try turning the cooler off and on
- The bedroom fan is making a funny noise, reset it
- Get the cold air going again in the hall

A daily medicine is a pill or drop that someone takes once a day, often at the same time. A dose is the amount to take. Doctors tell people how much and when, and the label on the box repeats it. People use their phone to help with this. They say, "Remind me to take my pill at eight," or "Change the reminder to nine." If a symptom comes back, they might ask, "Book a visit with my doctor." Sometimes a pill is too hard to swallow, and someone asks, "Can I pull the tablet in half?" That is a question for the doctor or the pharmacy, because the answer is on the page of the leaflet. A phone should never decide on a dose alone.

Ayesha was a busy mother of three, and on Saturday she wanted to take her son on a bike ride before the rain came. She put her phone in her pocket and rolled the bike out of the garage, under the roof of the shed.
"Find me a bike route to the lake. I don't want hills, and I don't want busy roads," she said.
The assistant thought for a second. It found a flat path along the river, six miles long, with a quiet park at the end. "This route is mostly north of the town," it said. "Shall I start the directions?"
"Yes, and tell me how far we have gone every two miles," said Ayesha. The assistant started and called out the distance, and her son rang his bell at each one.

Learning a language is a bit like learning to ride a bike. You start slowly and practice often. Many people take a lesson once a week and use their phones to help in between. They say, "How do you say good morning in Spanish?" or "Translate this sign for me." If a word is hard, they ask, "How do you spell it?" or "Say it again, slower." Travelers may say, "Teach me five useful phrases." Before they buy a ticket in another country, they like to know a few words. A thin phrase book can fit in a pocket, but a phone is faster. When they have learned a phrase, they say, "Save it to my list," so they can practice it later.

name: move_money
does: Moves a sum of money from one of your own accounts to another, such as from savings to checking, and can double the usual amount if you ask.
inputs: the account to take it from, the account to put it in, and how much
people say:
- Put fifty dollars from savings into checking
- Send my usual amount to the holiday fund
- I need more in my checking account
- Move everything above two hundred to savings
- Do the same transfer as last month, but double

Lei was a student with a tight budget and a big appetite. On Friday night, she wanted to eat out with friends, but she did not want to go to a place that cost too much. She picked up her phone on the public bus.
"Find a noodle place nearby that is cheaper than the last one we went to," she said.
The assistant showed three places. It said the second one was half the price of the last restaurant, and it had a farm theme with a painting of a cow on the wall. "Do you want to book a table?" it asked. Lei said yes, for four people at seven.
"Heat the leftovers at home first, so I don't come hungry," joked Lei. The assistant said it could not heat food, but it booked the table. Lei grinned and got off the bus.

People want the air in a room to get fresher, because they cannot open the windows, and the black dust on the shelf and the smell of glue are bothering them.
Fresh air, please
Turn on the air purifier
It smells in here
Can you run the ventilation fan for half an hour?
The air feels dry, switch on the humidifier
Please reply with the current air quality in the bedroom
Could you please start the purifier in the living room? My son has asthma and I just painted the furniture, so I want the air to be clean before he comes home.
I would be very grateful if you could keep the fan on all night, because the smell from the new carpet is giving me a headache.

Bjorn woke up on the sofa with a stiff neck. The room was gray, and on the screen of his phone a podcast was still paused. He had fallen asleep while listening, and he could not remember where he stopped.
"Where did I fall asleep?" he mumbled.
The assistant said he had been listening to a history podcast about old bridges, and he stopped at minute thirty-one of episode nine. It asked if he wanted to find the last part he remembered. Bjorn said, "Go back four minutes." The assistant went back and played from there.
He listened while he made coffee. When the host talked about a meter-long stone, he laughed. "Play the next four episodes in a row," he said. The assistant lined up the next four, and Bjorn stretched his arms and drank his coffee.

Television shows you channels, movies and streaming programs, and you control it with a remote. Most people use a few simple words to ask for things. They say, "Turn on the news," "Change to channel five," or "Louder, please." If a show is hard to follow, they ask for subtitles. Before a holiday, a family might say, "Record the holiday movie for Saturday night." When the list of saved shows gets long, they say, "Remove the old shows." Someone who is polite may even say, "Could you please pause it for a minute?" The remote has buttons for all of this, but many people now find it easier to simply talk.
